title: Attributing a Toll to a Driver's Detour by Route Length (Wayfare Rides)
content:
On a detoured trip of **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)**, the toll attributed to the driver's detour is worked out from how far the route ran beyond the estimate, measured as the trip's actual miles divided by its estimated miles. The toll is the toll charge amount booked on the trip.

## Rule

| Actual miles divided by estimated miles | Attributed toll |
|---|---|
| at least 1.75 (severe detour ratio) | the whole toll charged on the trip |
| at least 1.25 (moderate detour ratio) and below 1.75 | the part of the toll in proportion to the extra miles: the toll multiplied by the actual miles less the estimated miles, divided by the actual miles |
| below 1.25 | not set by route length |

A ratio of at least 1.75 attributes the whole toll charged on the trip to the detour. A ratio of at least 1.25 but below 1.75 attributes the part of the toll charged in proportion to the extra miles, that is the toll times the actual miles less the estimated miles, divided by the actual miles; this figure is not rounded. Below 1.25, the attributed toll is not set by route length.

## Worked cases (hypothetical trips, toll $4.30)

| Estimated miles | Actual miles | Ratio | Attributed toll |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10.0 | 18.0 | 1.8 | $4.30, the whole toll |
| 10.0 | 17.5 | 1.75 | $4.30 — exactly the severe ratio |
| 10.0 | 14.0 | 1.4 | $4.30 multiplied by 4.0 extra miles, divided by 14.0 actual miles: $1.228571… (unrounded) |
| 10.0 | 12.5 | 1.25 | $4.30 multiplied by 2.5, divided by 12.5: $0.86 |
| 10.0 | 12.4 | 1.24 | not set by route length |
